title: Theory of ion and water transport in reverse osmosis membranes
authors: Y. S. Oren, P. M. Biesheuvel
abstract: We present theory for ion and water transport through reverse osmosis membranes based on a Maxwell-Stefan framework combined with hydrodynamic theory for the reduced motion of particles in thin pores. We include all driving forces and frictions both on the fluid (water), and on the ions, including ion-fluid friction as well as ion-wall friction. By including the acid-base character of the carbonic acid system, the boric acid system, H3O+/OH-, and the membrane charge, we locally determine pH and thus the effective charge of the membrane as well as the dissociation degree of boric acid. We present calculation results for a dead end experiment with fixed feed concentration, where effluent composition is a self-consistent function of fluxes through the membrane. Comparison with experimental results from literature for fluid flow vs. pressure, and for salt and boron rejection, shows that theory agrees well with data. Our model is based on realistic assumptions for the effective sizes of the ions and for the diameter of the RO membrane pore in the polyamide toplayer (≈0.75 nm).

analysis_results.limitations: While the study provides valuable theoretical insights into water molecule dissociation on graphene and its doped variants, it does not address practical implementation challenges or experimental validation of the computational models.
analysis_results.methodology: Density functional theory calculations were employed to investigate the adsorption energies of H2O molecules and their dissociated fragments (H and OH) on various two-dimensional substrates including graphene and its doped variants. The methodology includes detailed computational analysis to understand charge distribution and atomic interactions, providing insights into the mechanisms governing water dissociation and transport at the molecular level.
analysis_results.key_findings: The study reveals that graphene doped with nitrogen exhibits the highest stability for water molecule dissociation, offering a promising platform for enhancing proton conductivity in electromembrane systems.
analysis_results.rolling_summary: This research explores water molecule dissociation on various two-dimensional substrates, including graphene and its doped variants (graphene-doped with B, N, C), focusing on their potential applications in electromembrane systems for efficient transport phenomena. The study employs density functional theory calculations to investigate the adsorption energies of H2O molecules and their dissociated fragments (H and OH) on these substrates. Key findings reveal that graphene doped with nitrogen exhibits the highest stability for water molecule dissociation, offering a promising platform for enhancing proton conductivity in electromembrane systems. The methodology includes detailed computational analysis to understand charge distribution and atomic interactions, providing insights into the mechanisms governing water dissociation and transport at the molecular level.
analysis_results.russian_analysis_summary: Исследование предоставляет теоретические данные по расщеплению водных молекул на графене и его модифицированных вариантах, что может быть полезно для улучшения транспортировки в электромембранной системе. Однако отсутствуют практические испытания или экспериментальная проверка модели.
analysis_results.relevance_to_water_splitting: The research focuses on the potential applications of these findings in electromembrane systems for efficient transport phenomena, particularly enhancing proton conductivity through optimized substrate materials.
analysis_results.russian_translation_of_abstract: Это исследование изучает расщепление молекул воды на различных двухмерных подложках, включая графен и его модифицированные варианты (графен, дoped с B, N, C), акцентируя внимание на их потенциальных приложениях в электромембранной системе для эффективного транспорта. Исследование использует расчеты теории функционала плотности для изучения энергий адсорбции молекул H2O и их диссоциированных фрагментов (H и OH) на этих подложках. Основные результаты показывают, что графен, модифицированный азотом, демонстрирует наибольшую устойчивость для расщепления молекул воды, предлагая перспективную платформу для повышения проводимости протонов в электромембранной системе. Методология включает детальный вычислительный анализ для понимания распределения зарядов и атомных взаимодействий, предоставляя представление о механизмах, управляющих расщеплением воды и транспортом на молекулярном уровне.
